spec_basis: STU-VID-033: 'Multicam is a clip mode, not a separate editor. A multicam source sequence holds N synchronised angles; a clip referencing it exposes an `active_angle` that is switchable over time, producing a cut list.'
STU-VID-033: 'Angle count is at least 16 in the addressable command surface; Studio imposes no fixed maximum beyond a document performance budget.'
STU-VID-033: 'Two switch modes: switch WITH a cut (creates an edit at the playhead and changes the angle after it) and switch WITHOUT a cut (changes the angle for the whole clip).'
STU-VID-033: 'A record mode captures live angle switches during playback into a cut list; toggling record is a single command.'
STU-VID-033: 'A preview surface shows all angles in a paged grid with first/last/next/previous page navigation, next/previous angle, and next/previous edit navigation.'
STU-VID-033: '`audio_follows_video` is a boolean: when true an angle switch also switches the audio.'
STU-VID-033: '`flatten` bakes the current cut list into ordinary clips and discards the multicam mode; it is one reversible history step.'
STU-VID-033: 'A selection-order option (top-down versus source order) decides angle numbering.'
STU-VID-030a: 'multicam clips MAY be set to follow or ignore the nest setting. Both are explicit booleans on the nested clip, never implicit.'
STU-VID-040: 'A multicam record pass is one step.'

STU-VID-041 command ids carried in receipts: cmd.clip.create.multicam, cmd.clip.multicam.flatten, cmd.clip.multicam.toggle, cmd.multicam.choose.camera.N, cmd.multicam.choosenocut.cameraN, cmd.multicam.toggle.record, cmd.multicam.audio.follows.video, cmd.multicam.follows.nest.setting, cmd.multicam.page.first|last|next|previous, cmd.multicam.next.camera, cmd.multicam.previous.camera, cmd.multicam.next.edit, cmd.multicam.prev.edit, cmd.multicam.selection.top.down
declared_readings: one angle = one VIDEO track of the source sequence; angle n's audio = the audio track with the same per-kind index (none = silent angle)
selection order: source_order = ascending video track index, top_down = descending index; angle_order is derived and validated, never free
audio_angle stored separately; equals active_angle while audio_follows_video; turning audio_follows_video on aligns audio_angle to active_angle
a multicam clip on a video track shows active_angle, on an audio track plays audio_angle
enabled=false plays the source as an ordinary nest and keeps the angles; enabling a nest without a mode gives angle 1, audio_follows_video on, follow-nest off
record pass: event at the clip's first tick switches without a cut, later events cut
flatten: pieces unlinked, no markers, head/tail transition kept only where a piece starts/ends with the clip, else dropped and listed; clips with markers refused multicam_markers_present
unit forward speed only for resolve/flatten (multicam_speed_unsupported otherwise)
paging and next/previous angle clamp at the ends (no wrap)
spec_deltas: STU-VID-033 does not specify angle sync on creation (audio waveform, timecode, in points): lane accepts caller offsets and in points, refuses timecode and audio waveform with multicam_sync_unsupported
STU-VID-033 does not specify the angle <-> track mapping or the audio pairing (declared: video track per angle, audio by same index)
STU-VID-033 does not specify defaults of audio_follows_video or selection order, nor how audio behaves when audio_follows_video is off (declared: separate audio_angle)
STU-VID-033 does not specify the meaning of top-down vs source order in a Studio document (declared: descending vs ascending video track index)
STU-VID-033 does not specify flatten of speed-changed angles, markers or transitions
